Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: some pronouns ar marked in absolutive with ke

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: 1SG absolutive: i-ke; 1SG ergative: e-ra. All persons have distinct ergative forms with suffix -ra. Full ergative-absolutive alignment on all independent pronouns.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: 2SG absolutive: mi-ke; 2SG ergative: mi-ra. Ergative suffix -ra added to all 2nd person forms (sg, dl, pl).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: 3SG absolutive: tu-ke; 3SG ergative: tu-ra. All 3rd person forms (sg, dl, pl, proximal) have ergative counterparts with -ra.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs in A function take enclitic =ra (ERG). S and O NPs are unmarked. Consistent ergative-absolutive alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative marking applies consistently across all TAM categories. No split conditioned by aspect. Both imperfective (ex. 2a) and other aspects show ergative marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative marking applies in perfective/completive contexts. No TAM-conditioned split reported.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Ergative =ra appears in recent past (ex. 1a: iye-chine) and remote past (kware) contexts alike. No tense-conditioned split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Ergative marking present in imperfective/non-past contexts (ex. 2a: adeba-ya 'know-IMPFV'). No split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: Main declarative clauses consistently show ergative marking. No mood-conditioned split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Dependent clauses (imperative, hortative, conditional, etc.) also show ergative case marking on A arguments (ex. 20, 21a). No split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Realis contexts show consistent ergative marking. No realis/irrealis split reported.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Conditional/irrealis clauses also show ergative marking (ex. 21c: i-ke in absolutive, e-ra in ergative). No split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Ergative marking is not conditioned by semantic agentivity. All A arguments receive =ra regardless of agentivity.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: No agentivity-conditioned split reported. Ergative marking applies uniformly.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality-conditioned split reported. Ergative marking is not sensitive to discourse-pragmatic factors.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No topicality-conditioned split. Ergative marking applies uniformly regardless of topicality.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: No animacy-conditioned split reported. Ergative marking applies to animate and inanimate A arguments alike.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No animacy-conditioned split. Ergative marking applies uniformly.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Main clauses consistently show ergative marking on A NPs and pronouns. This is the primary domain of the ergative pattern.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: All dependent clause types (non-finite and finite) show ergative case marking on A arguments, with the exception of general purpose clauses where A receives genitive marking (still an ergative-based system). No S/O pivot found in dependent clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by other factors?
Comment: Guillaume explicitly concludes there is NO split ergativity in Cavineña morphology. The apparent split reported by Camp (1985) is due to a morpho-phonological rule of suffix deletion (-ra and -ke deletion), not a morpho-syntactic split. At the syntactic level, co-reference constraints in dependent clauses operate on a NOMINATIVE-ACCUSATIVE basis (S/A pivot), not ergative.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the genitive marker?
Comment: The ergative marker =ra (NPs) / -ra (pronouns) is DISTINCT from the genitive marker -ja (e.g. e-kwe 'my', tata-chi=ja 'father's'). In general purpose dependent clauses, A receives genitive marking -ja, but this is a distinct morpheme from the ergative =ra.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the instrumental/comitative marker?
Comment: The ergative marker =ra is distinct from instrumental and comitative markers. No syncretism between ergative and instrumental/comitative reported for Cavineña (contrast with Panoan languages like Matses/SK where -n marks ERG=GEN=INST).
